title: Joan Laporta elected president
detail: Beat the favourite, Lluís Bassat, on the back of a promise to sign David Beckham. A later court ruling dated his presidency from June 2003.
people: Joan Laporta; Lluís Bassat; David Beckham
evidence: In the 2003 elections, Laporta did not start as the favourite, but his charisma grew during the electoral campaign and he finally won against the expected victor, publicist Lluís Bassat, in part because of a widely published (and ultimately unfulfilled) promise to bring David Beckham to Barcelona.

title: Laporta's young board
detail: A new, young and largely untested board, with Sandro Rosell among its backers.
evidence: Laporta had the support of other young businessmen of Barcelona, such as Sandro Rosell.

title: Frank Rijkaard appointed head coach
detail: Less than a year after leaving Sparta Rotterdam (relegated). Assistants Albert Roca and Henk ten Cate. The source gives no exact date.
people: Frank Rijkaard; Albert Roca; Henk ten Cate
evidence: Rijkaard was not out of a coaching role for long, and less than a year after leaving Sparta, he was appointed manager of Barcelona for the 2003–04 season, with Albert Roca and Henk ten Cate as assistants.

title: Beckham goes to Real Madrid instead
detail: Laporta's campaign promise falls through and fans blame the new board.
evidence: Rijkaard arrived at the club as it entered a new phase, having elected a new president in Joan Laporta and a new managerial board, but with fans unhappy that Laporta had let English midfielder David Beckham snub the chance to join the club.

title: Txiki Begiristain becomes director of football
detail: Former Dream Team winger joins Laporta's board as director of football.
evidence: After retiring as a player, Begiristain worked as a commentator for Televisió de Catalunya before becoming director of football at former club Barcelona in 2003.

title: Ronaldinho signs from Paris Saint-Germain
detail: Second choice after Beckham (and Henry). Barcelona outbid Manchester United in a deal of about €30m. Transfermarkt dates the move 19 July 2003; the BBC reported it on 20 July. The club season page lists the fee as €27M.
evidence: Henry remained with Arsenal, and Laporta then promised to bring Beckham to the club, but following his transfer to Real Madrid, Barcelona entered the running for Ronaldinho and outbid Manchester United for his signature in a €30 million deal.

title: Ronaldinho's first game for Barcelona
detail: Friendly against Juventus at Gillette Stadium, Foxborough (USA tour).
evidence: Ronaldinho made his Barcelona debut in a friendly against Juventus at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts on 27 July, with coach Frank Rijkaard stating post match, "He has something special every time he touches the ball."

title: In the UEFA Cup — not the Champions League
detail: First season outside the Champions League since 1995–96 (6th in 2002–03).
evidence: Barcelona competed in the UEFA Cup rather than the UEFA Champions League for the first time since the 1995–96 season, given their sixth-place finish in 2002–03.

title: Ronaldinho's first competitive goal — at 1:30 a.m.
detail: From inside his own half, past two Sevilla players, a 30-yard shot in off the crossbar. Round 2, played after midnight.
evidence: He scored his first competitive goal in La Liga on 3 September 2003 against Sevilla at 1.30 a.m.

title: Big win: Barcelona 8–0 Matador Púchov
detail: UEFA Cup First round, second leg

title: Lionel Messi's first-team debut, aged 16
detail: Came on in the 75th minute of the friendly at Porto (Porto 2–0 Barça). In the same season he played for four youth teams.
evidence: At 16 years old, Messi made his first-team debut when he came on in the 75th minute during a friendly against FC Porto on 16 November 2003.

title: Rijkaard under fire after the Camp Nou Clásico
detail: Fans call for his resignation; the media turn on him after losing 1–2 to Real Madrid.
evidence: Rijkaard had a disappointing start at Barcelona that saw some sections of the club's fans call for his resignation, and he drew flak from the media when the team lost to Real Madrid in December 2003.

title: El Clásico: Barcelona 1–2 Real Madrid
detail: For: Kluivert 83'; against: Roberto Carlos 37'; Ronaldo 73'

title: Laporta pleads for patience
detail: The old guard is phased out while the team is rebuilt around Ronaldinho.
evidence: To exacerbate the situation, the 2003–04 season began abysmally results-wise, with Laporta constantly having to call for the fans' understanding and patience with him and Rijkaard as the club slowly phased out underachieving players from the old guard in order to rebuild a new-look side around Ronaldinho.

title: Big win: Ciudad de Murcia 0–4 Barcelona
Competitive debut: Oriol Riera (signed)
detail: came on 77' v Ciudad de Murcia

title: Edgar Davids arrives on loan from Juventus
detail: After tension with Lippi at Juventus. Debut on 17 Jan v Athletic; the unbeaten run had begun on 11 Jan. Widely cited as the catalyst for the turnaround.
evidence: Following some tensions with Juventus manager Lippi, as well as competition from new arrivals for a starting spot at Juventus during the first half of the 2003-04 season, Davids joined Barcelona on loan in January 2004.

title: Davids, the catalyst
evidence: Davids' arrival has been cited as the catalyst for the Catalan club's dominance of Spanish and European football during the mid-to-late 2000s (decade), with Barcelona winning La Liga the following season (after five years without winning the league title) and a La Liga and Champions League double in 2005–06.

title: Low point: 12th after round 18
detail: Racing de Santander 3–0 Barcelona; 18 pts behind the leader, 6 above the relegation places

title: Heavy defeat: Racing de Santander 3–0 Barcelona
Longest league winning run begins (9 wins)
Out of the Copa del Rey: Zaragoza 1–1 Barcelona
Out of the UEFA Cup: Barcelona 0–0 Celtic
Xavi wins it at the Bernabéu
detail: Ronaldinho's scooped pass sets up the winner: the club's first win at the Bernabéu in seven years, and the start of "the Barcelona rise" in Xavi's words.
evidence: His scooped pass set up the winning goal for Xavi away to Real Madrid on 25 April 2004, the club's first win at the Bernabéu in seven years, a result Xavi credits as the start of "the Barcelona rise".

title: Real Madrid lose their last five
detail: Top at the halfway mark and still top after round 31. Stuck on 70 pts from round 33, they end 4th and hand Valencia the title. Barça pass them in round 37 (16 May).
evidence: They also lost their final five La Liga matches and finished in fourth place, which gave Valencia the title.

title: The turnaround
detail: Runners-up after being close to the relegation zone earlier in the season.
evidence: Barcelona finished runners-up in La Liga in 2003–04, having been close to the relegation zone at one point in the earlier stages of the season.

title: Valencia win the double
detail: Benítez's Valencia win La Liga and the UEFA Cup.
evidence: Valencia CF enjoyed a marvellous season by winning the La Liga and UEFA Cup double.

title: BBC documentary: FC Barcelona Confidential
detail: The BBC filmed the season after Laporta's arrival.
evidence: The BBC made a documentary, titled FC Barcelona Confidential, based on the turn of events in the league after Joan Laporta's entry.
